claims.text: Nanoparticles containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios have high configurational entropy when present as a disordered solid solution.
High configurational entropy maintains the structural and chemical stability of these nanoparticles throughout 473–1923 K.
Temperature is varied over the range 473–1923 K.
The prediction is conditioned on the nanoparticles retaining a random disordered solid solution without intermetallic compounds.
The structural mediator is a disordered solid solution with high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy reduces the thermodynamic driving force for phase separation and ordering.
Reduction of the thermodynamic driving force for separation and ordering preserves structural and chemical stability.
The nanoparticles will show no significant phase separation or ordering over 473–1923 K.
The initial baseline is a high-configurational-entropy disordered solid solution.
Stability may be compromised above 1923 K.
The relationship between configurational entropy and stability is not fully understood because mixing enthalpy, diffusion, and kinetic constraints may also affect stability.
Heating above 1923 K followed by X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy can test for structural and compositional changes.
Significant phase separation or ordering after heat treatment above 1923 K would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is bounded to 473–1923 K and explicitly allows stability to be compromised above 1923 K, yet the proposed falsification experiment tests only above 1923 K and treats instability there as falsifying. An outcome outside the stated validity range cannot falsify the bounded prediction.
